papers.title: An elementary proof of rational injectivity in equivariant KK-theory
papers.abstract: Antonini, Azzali and Skandalis proved that, for every countable discrete group $\Gamma$, the canonical map $E\Gamma\to\underline{E}\Gamma$ induces a split injection in equivariant $KK$-theory with real coefficients. In this paper, we give a more elementary proof of the corresponding rational injectivity result in ordinary equivariant $KK$-theory without using $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors.

papers.title: A K\"unneth theorem for the cyclic homology of A-infinity algebras
papers.abstract: The cyclic homology of a $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-graded, smooth and proper $A_\infty$ category satisfying the Hodge-to-de-Rham degeneration property carries the structure of a polarized semi-infinite Hodge structure or the so-called EP-structure. Given two $A_\infty$ algebras $A$ and $B$ with the above conditions, we construct a K\"unneth map from the tensor product of their cyclic homologies to the cyclic homology of the $A_\infty$ tensor product $A\otimes_\infty B$ and show that it respects the EP-structures. As an application, we show that if $A$ and $B$ are equipped with weak Calabi-Yau structures, then $A\otimes_\infty B$ also inherits a weak Calabi-Yau structure. Also, we show that the K\"unneth quasi-isomorphism respects good splittings of the Hodge filtration on $A$ and $B$ compatible with the weak Calabi-Yau structure. Our explicit calculations rely on the combinatorial (tree) description of the tensor product of $A_\infty$ algebras developed in \cite{amorim2016tensor}.

papers.title: Geometric chains of orbifolds with corners and singular homology
papers.abstract: We study a geometric homology theory (GHT for short). Its chains are generated by smooth maps from compact oriented orbifolds with corners to a smooth space, and two kinds of chains are set to zero: those admitting an orientation reversing automorphism, and degenerate ones, which, together with their boundaries, factor through smooth maps to orbifolds of lower dimension. Bisecting the source of a geometric chain along a hypersurface transverse to its corners changes the chain only by the boundary of an explicit prism and by prisms over its faces; cutting a geometric cycle along a regular level set of a smooth function on the target does not change its homology class. Geometric chains also behave well under products and pullbacks along fibre bundles, which overcomes some of the combinatorial rigidity of singular chains. We prove that geometric homology is naturally isomorphic to singular homology with rational coefficients for every smooth space admitting a good cover, such as smooth manifolds, orbifolds and locally finite polyhedra, and also for orbifolds with corners. The proof uses cutting operators along level sets of functions on the target, realized by explicit prisms, instead of triangulations. For continuous maps into arbitrary spaces we conjecture the same statement, and prove it for Euclidean neighbourhood retracts in degrees at most one, with surjectivity in degree two. Without the relation killing degenerate chains the comparison fails for orbifold chains: the weighted projective plane $\mathbb{P}(1,1,p)$, $p\ge5$ prime, mapped to a point is a cycle that does not bound. Applications on Morse theory and the BV structure on geometric chains of moduli spaces of bordered Riemann surfaces, following Costello and Harrelson--Voronov--Z\'u\~niga, are given.

papers.title: Isogenies of Oriented Elliptic Curves
papers.abstract: We construct and describe the moduli stack $\mathrm{Isog}$ of isogenies between oriented elliptic curves. We show that $\mathrm{Isog}$ is a spectral Deligne-Mumford stack and a relative spectral algebraic space over $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{ell}}^{\mathrm{or}}$, and give a fiber product decomposition of $\mathrm{Isog}$ corresponding to a connected-\'etale factorization on oriented elliptic curves. In the process of proving these results, we construct a theory of duality and quotients for spectral abelian varieties, prove a higher-algebraic version of Nakayama's lemma, and lift the rigidity theorem for morphisms of elliptic curves to the setting of spectral algebraic geometry.

papers.title: Localizing Restriction Categories
papers.abstract:
The localizing/separating factorization, which is the analogue, for restriction categories, to the surjective/embedding factorization for topoi, is developed at both the mere restriction category and join restriction category level. The factorization system at both the ordinary and join level is approached using the notion of a density, which is a stable and universal suborder of the restriction order. The main technical results of the paper construct the join localization and establish its basic properties. 
  The paper gives several examples of localizations. In particular, examples of localization on commutative rigs are provided which give a way to construct categories of schemes. The Zariski spectrum and the Pierce spectrum are, in particular, developed.

papers.title: Bridging persistence of discrete and continuous 1D maps: Total variation, permutation equivalence, and diagonal affine transformations
papers.abstract: Fundamental to the field of topological signal processing (TSP) is the \textit{persistence diagram} (PD), or barcode, of a signal, which gives noise-resistant measures of topologically significant features as distinct from noise. Existing literature proves that the total persistence computed from these diagrams is equal to the total variation, for certain continuous signals on compact domains. We provide a closed formula for this shared quantity, and generalize to all continuous and discrete functions on bounded domains, and to certain functions on non-compact 1D manifolds. Extending the identification of continuous and discrete persistence, we investigate the similarities of functions with the same PDs, and prove that, for any $n$, the persistence diagram can be calculated as a function of the sequence of critical values; we compute these formulas for $n \leq 6$. Finally, we examine which function transformations cause predictable changes in the PD of the transformed function, characterizing affine and linear transformations.

papers.title: Inscribed Square Problem and an Embedding of M¨obius Band in a Family of Solid Toruses
papers.abstract: In this paper, we relate the space of line segments induced by a Jordan curve in the plane to the space of line segments induced by the plane by embedding the M¨obius band associated with the curve into the family of toruses associated with the plane; we further demonstrate how the geometric ”square condition” of the curve translates into a topological property through this embedding.

papers.title: Landfall Geometry
papers.abstract: We study the negative gradient flow of analytic maps $f:X\to\R$ defined on compact analytic Riemannian manifolds without imposing any nondegeneracy or transversality assumptions. We construct tight isolating blocks around the connected components of the critical set $\Crit(f)$ and record only bounded-time contacts made after an orbit exits one block and before it makes landfall within the interior of another. These contacts assemble into a strict topological category $\cL$ -- called the landfall category -- whose classifying space $B\cL$ is shown to be simple homotopy equivalent to $X$ naturally over all down-sets of the flow partial order. The filtered homotopy type is independent of the isolating blocks. Passing to a finite subanalytic triangulation yields a flow-induced acyclic partial matching, and hence, an explicit finite chain complex generated by the non-exit simplices of the blocks which computes the homology of $X$. The finite model also computes the Morse--Conley spectral sequence over arbitrary coefficients; over a field, homological perturbation further produces a connection matrix whose entries are finite sums over descending contact itineraries.

papers.title: Mathematical AI Predicts 40% and 57% Influenza Vaccine Effectiveness Against H1N1 and H3N2, Respectively, for the 2026--2027 U.S. Season
papers.abstract:
Background: Clinical influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) has often been low over the past two decades, highlighting the need for preseason VE forecasting. Timely forecasts could help health authorities plan prevention strategies and allocate healthcare resources. However, preseason forecasting of clinical influenza VE remains relatively uncommon.
  Methods: We obtained hemagglutinin (HA) sequences from GISAID for U.S. specimens collected in August--September before each influenza season from 2010--2011 through 2024--2025. After quality screening, we compared each virus with the corresponding vaccine target strain for the same season and subtype or lineage using two mathematical distances based on amino acid patterns in the HA protein. We calculated mean distances for each season and subtype or lineage and paired them with published clinical VE estimates, yielding 26 observations across 13 seasons. Using a mathematical AI approach, we fitted linear regression models of VE against each distance and evaluated their predictive performance by forecasting later seasons using data from earlier seasons, with the historical mean VE for each subtype or lineage as a reference. We then applied the same approach to 87 HA sequences collected in August--September 2026 to forecast VE for the 2026--2027 season.
  Results: We generated component-specific forecasts of influenza VE for the upcoming 2026--2027 U.S. season. Both mathematical distances were negatively associated with historical VE, indicating that greater differences between circulating viruses and vaccine strains were associated with lower VE. The topological model forecast VE of 40.3%, 56.9%, and 47.1% against A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B/Victoria, respectively, whereas the geometric model forecast corresponding VE values of 34.0%, 56.8%, and 51.1%.

papers.title: The center is the formal internal automorphism group
papers.abstract: We prove that the deformation functor associated to an algebra over a sufficiently nice Koszul operad can be lifted to an operadic formal moduli problem over the Koszul dual operad. We further show that this operadic formal moduli problem corresponds to the derived center of the algebra under the operadic Lurie-Pridham correspondence. As an application, we prove that the classical Gerstenhaber algebra structure on polyvector fields of a commutative algebra agrees with the derived center of the algebra as an abelian Poisson algebra.

papers.title: Triangulation of orbifolds with corners
papers.abstract: We prove that every compact orbifold with corners admits a triangulation in which the image of every codimension one face is a subcomplex. Faces need not be embedded, and the local groups may permute boundary components. The proof turns the boundary hyperplanes of linear charts into mirrors by means of the squaring map, which, unlike the folding $y\mapsto|y|$, is compatible with smooth changes of charts, and then applies the triangulation theorem for orbit spaces of proper Lie groupoids.

papers.title: Vanishing of Higher Magnitude Homology for Finite Prefix Models
papers.abstract: Bradley and Vigneaux define a generalized distance on a finite prefix poset using next-token probabilities. They conjecture that its higher magnitude homology vanishes. Motivated by their expression of magnitude as a weighted sum of homological Euler characteristics, we verify this conjecture for their explicit complex, in which both endpoint faces are zero. For each finite length, the homology groups in degrees two and above are zero. The degree-one homology group is free abelian, with one generator for each positive-probability edge of that length. The proof constructs a contracting homotopy for each component whose endpoints have an interior prefix. This homotopy inserts the least interior prefix. Edge probabilities zero and one are both allowed.

papers.title: $\mathbb{A}^1$-connectedness of moduli of vector bundles on a stacky curve
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{C}$ be a projective stacky curve over an infinite field $k$ with the coarse space $C$, a geometrically connected smooth projective curve, together with a generating sheaf $\mathcal{E}$ on $\mathfrak{C}$. We consider the moduli stack of $\mathcal{E}$-semistable vector bundles of fixed determinant and multiplicities on $\mathfrak{C}$, and show that it is $\mathbb{A}^1$-connected if and only if it admits a $k$-rational point. We show that this holds whenever genus of $C$ is at least $2$ and $C(k)\neq \emptyset$. As a consequence, we conclude that, for any system of weights $\boldsymbol{\alpha}$, the moduli stack of parabolic $\boldsymbol{\alpha}$-semistable vector bundles of fixed determinant and quasi-parabolic data on a geometrically connected smooth projective curve is $\mathbb{A}^1$-connected.

papers.title: $\SL_3$ dual pairs
papers.abstract: We study the exceptional theta correspondence for dual pairs of the form $\SL_3\times G$ inside $p$-adic groups of type $E_n$, $n=6,7,8$. We establish Howe duality for lifts of all Whittaker-generic unitarizable representations of $\SL_3$. Our dual pair is in a see-saw relationship with a dual pair of the form $G_2 \times H$ such that $G/H$ is a rank-two symmetric space. Using the theta correspondence for $\SL_3 \times G$, we prove a multiplicity-one result for $H$-invariant functionals on representations of $G$.

papers.title: A 15/16 zero-free half-plane for angular Hecke L-functions over the Eisenstein field
papers.abstract: We describe the argument recorded in a frozen Lean development for nonvanishing of the unit-compatible angular Hecke L-functions over \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})\) in the strict half-plane \(\Re(s)>15/16\), apart from the genuine principal pole. The family includes imprimitive finite parts, every integer angular type allowed by the unit relation, and real unitary norm twists. The proof route passes through a mean-square estimate for the actual sextic rows, sixth-power averaging, a smoothed Möbius estimate with a totient factor, and Mellin continuation. We reconstruct the angular reflection, quadratic energy estimate, finite descent, and the calculation producing the \(15/16\) exponent, while identifying the technical source lemmas inherited from OAI-003 that remain to be independently reconstructed. The theorem is formally verified in Lean and the frozen source/evidence package has undergone statement comparison, axiom audit, recursive kernel replay, quotient postchecking, and separate AI-assisted review. This manuscript is an expository reconstruction rather than a claim of independent human certification. We describe the formally verified proof as a xenoproof, and the theorem provisionally as a xenotheorem, to distinguish formal mathematical correctness from human mathematical understanding.

papers.title: A 256-step certificate for Turán's pure power-sum constant
papers.abstract: We give an exact-input certificate for the upper bound C_42 <= 0.6888863712 in the pure power-sum problem. The construction refines the step profiles of Griego, Röhrig and Plata to 256 middle blocks, without changing their coefficient-cancellation mechanism. It improves the strongest public proposal located in our 22 October 2026 audit, 0.688970, by 0.0000836288. An unmodified public interval checker and a separately written Arb checker verify the strict finite inequalities. The asymptotic implication is proved in the note; no explicit finite threshold, optimality, human peer review or formal verification is claimed.

papers.title: A counterexample to Liu's conjecture on Fano indices in dimension four
papers.abstract: We prove that Liu's conjecture on Fano indices fails in dimension four: $1389$ is the index of a terminal Calabi--Yau fourfold and of a four-dimensional log canonical singularity, but it is not the Fano index of any canonical weighted projective space of dimension four.

papers.title: A counterexample to the table conjecture on the sphere
papers.abstract: We disprove Matschke's table conjecture, which asserts that every continuous real-valued function on $S^2$ takes a common value on the vertices of some rotated copy of every prescribed inscribed square. The counterexample is the cubic polynomial $H(x,y,z)=14z^3-6z+y+xz$ and a square contained in a plane at distance $1/\sqrt{7}$ from the origin. We give an elementary proof.

papers.title: A polynomial algorithm for general d-position in trees
papers.abstract: A vertex set is in general $d$-position if no three of its vertices lie on a shortest path of length at most $d$. We give an exact algorithm for an $n$-vertex tree in $O(n(D+2)^4)$ time and $O(n(D+2)^2)$ space, where $D=\min\{d,n-1\}$. In particular, the problem is polynomial-time solvable when the threshold is part of the input. This answers the tree-complexity question posed by Klav\v zar, Rall, and Yero in 2021 and retained in the August 2026 version of the general position survey. The dynamic program uses two truncated distances at each rooted boundary: the nearest selected vertex and the nearest far endpoint of an ancestor-comparable selected pair. These distances characterize every forbidden triple created by joining child subtrees. The algorithm reconstructs an optimal set and extends to signed vertex weights and exact counting of optimal sets. It also computes the full cardinality generating polynomial in $O(n^2(D+2)^4)$ coefficient operations. Exhaustive comparisons with direct subset enumeration support the implementation independently of the proof.

papers.title: A quantitative refinement of Lu's elementary prime number theorem
papers.abstract: We refine Lu's elementary method for the prime number theorem to obtain, for every fixed $K>400$, \[ \psi(X)-X=O_K\!\left( X\exp\!\left\{-\frac{\sqrt{\log X}}{(\log\log X)^K}\right\}\right) \qquad(X\to\infty), \] where $\psi$ is Chebyshev's function. The main ingredient is a comparison estimate that remains uniform as the degree grows and the short-interval parameter shrinks. Combining this estimate with exponential weights in Balog's identity, a single finite energy step and positivity-based interpolation yields the stated bound, retaining the full degree tail and all arithmetic correction terms. The resulting remainder strengthens Lu's fixed-parameter estimates and Goz\'e's quantitative refinement within the real-variable framework; stronger remainder estimates are known by other methods.

papers.title: A semiampleness result for hyperk\"ahler fourfolds and smoothings of Lagrangian subvarieties
papers.abstract: We give a geometric proof of the following statement: let $X$ be a smooth hyperk\"ahler fourfold such that the Picard group is generated by a line bundle $L$ that is nef, non-trivial, and not big. If the Kodaira dimension of $L$ is non-negative, some positive multiple defines a Lagrangian fibration. The proof requires a number of tools which are of independent interest, including an analogue of Voisin's unobstructedness result and a smoothing result for singular Lagrangian subvarieties.

papers.title: A truncated theta-type series with triangular weights
papers.abstract: Merca (2026) recently introduced the two-block odd partition function $a(n)$, proved that its generating function factors as $A(q)=P(q)S(q)$, where $P(q)$ is the generating function of partitions whose odd parts are distinct and whose even parts are unrestricted and $S(q)$ is a theta-type series with triangular-number weights, and conjectured that for $N\equiv1,2\pmod 4$ the truncation $P(q)S_N(q)$ of this product has nonnegative coefficients, positive from $q^{3}$ onward. We prove the conjecture in the stronger form $P(q)S_N(q)-A(q)\in\NN[[q]]$.

papers.title: All $\tau_k$-maximal graphs have the same size
papers.abstract: A graph is $\tau_k$-maximal if none of its subgraphs has $k+1$ edge-disjoint spanning trees, but adding any missing edge creates such a subgraph. Wang and Tian conjectured that every $\tau_k$-maximal graph on $n\ge 2k+2$ vertices has exactly $(k+1)(n-1)-1$ edges. We prove this conjecture.

papers.title: Almost simple subgroups of the space Cremona group
papers.abstract: We prove that every finite almost simple subgroup that is not simple of the group of birational automorphisms of the three-dimensional complex projective space is isomorphic to one of the following: $\mathfrak{S}_5$, $\mathfrak{S}_6$, $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{F}_7)$ or $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{F}_9)$. We also prove that the group of birational automorphisms of the three-dimensional complex projective space contains unique (up to conjugation) subgroups isomorphic to $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{F}_7)$ and $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{F}_9)$.

papers.title: An asymptotic $\Gamma$-BMT inequality
papers.abstract: We refine a bound of Cheng-Feyzbakhsh to prove an asymptotic $\Gamma$-Bayer-Macr\`i-Toda ($\Gamma$-BMT) inequality on every smooth polarized complex threefold. The proof relies on a reduction to small tilt stability parameters. Using this inequality we verify Feyzbakhsh-Thomas's condition $(wBG)$ whenever $K_{X}$ is numerically proportional to the polarization. For polarized Calabi-Yau threefolds, this yields a reduction of positive rank generalized Donaldson-Thomas (DT) invariants to those counting sheaves pure in codimension one. We further express these invariants in terms of rank one generalized DT invariants. Thus, the rank reductions of Feyzbakhsh-Thomas hold without assuming the BMT conjecture.

papers.title: An explicit elementary proof of no Landau--Siegel zeros
papers.abstract: We give an elementary proof of the absence of Landau--Siegel zeros with the explicit constant $c=1/100$. For every primitive quadratic Dirichlet character $\chi$ of conductor $q\ge3$, each real zero $\beta\in(0,1)$ of $L(s,\chi)$ satisfies $(1-\beta)\log q>c$. The proof combines integer coefficient counting, polynomial congruences, a paired-tail hyperbola estimate, and a logarithmically weighted comparison of positive sums. All required constants are explicit, and one choice of parameters covers every conductor. The argument uses elementary arithmetic and real summation and integration, without separate zero computations for small conductors.

papers.title: An infinity-categorical TQFT from instantons
papers.abstract: In this paper, we lift the instanton TQFT from ordinary categories to the $\infty$-categorical setting by constructing a functor $CI:\mathrm{BI}^{\partial}\longrightarrow\mathsf{D}$ from an $\infty$-cobordism category $\mathrm{BI}^{\partial}$ for instantons to an $\infty$-derived category $\mathsf{D}$ of $2$-periodic chain complexes. The construction of $\mathrm{BI}^{\partial}$ is a modification of the $\infty$-cobordism category $\mathrm{Bord}_4$ introduced by Lurie and by Calaque--Scheimbauer using complete Segal spaces. The target $\infty$-category $\mathsf{D}$ is obtained via the dg nerve of the dg category of $2$-periodic chain complexes of finitely presented projective $\mathbb{Z}$-modules. The information encoded by the functor $CI$ was already developed by Kronheimer--Mrowka using families of metrics on cobordisms. Our reinterpretation in terms of $\infty$-categories conceptually simplifies the construction of the hypercube complexes underlying the link spectral sequence. This viewpoint also clarifies hyperbox complexes and compression in Manolescu--Ozsv\'{a}th's work, and possible $A_\infty$-structures, especially their signs and higher coherence. In addition, we lift the generalized cap product $\mu$-operators in instanton Floer homology to the chain level and construct explicit homotopies and higher homotopies establishing the commutativity of multiple $\mu$-operators in even degrees.

papers.title: Analytification and tropicalization via hyperfields and definable types
papers.abstract: We study the analytification and tropicalization of algebraic varieties over valued fields via Jun's spaces of hyperfield points. Our main new objects are a family of power-tropical hyperfields $H_n$ and their inverse limit $H$, recording at each level the class of a leading term modulo $n$-th powers of the residue field. They yield an enhanced tropicalization of the associated space $X(H)$, strictly finer than the Berkovich one exactly when the multiplicative group of the residue field is non-divisible: it specialises to the Berkovich analytification when the residue field is algebraically closed, to the real analytification of Jell-Scheiderer-Yu when it is real closed, and to a new $p$-adic analytification when it is $p$-adically closed. Over henselian valued fields of equicharacteristic $0$ we then construct a model-theoretic avatar of $X(H)$: the space $\widehat{X}_T$ of definable types orthogonal to the value group, which sharpens the geometry in the spirit of Hrushovski and Loeser and recovers their space over algebraically closed valued fields. We show that $\widehat{X}_T$ is strictly pro-definable, satisfies a model-theoretic Payne theorem, and definable compactness in such spaces satisfies a Heine-Borel type characterization. As an application, we analytify $p$-adic semi-algebraic sets and prove a strong density theorem for their tropicalizations, the exact $p$-adic counterpart of the real one of Jell-Scheiderer-Yu.

papers.title: Arithmetic of Jacobi polynomials
papers.abstract: We study the arithmetic of Jacobi polynomials. As applications, we prove the Mahlburg--Ono conjecture on the irreducibility and Galois groups of the four Kaneko--Zagier families, and the Cullinan--Hajir conjecture on the Galois groups of Legendre polynomials. Other applications concern common zeros of Jacobi polynomials, harmonic functions on cones, and hyperelliptic Jacobians.

papers.title: Aspects of quadratic Chabauty via modular forms
papers.abstract: We develop algorithms to construct a basis of de Rham cohomology for modular curves and a matrix representing the Hodge filtration required in the quadratic Chabauty method. We do this without requiring an explicit plane model of the curve and instead compute these objects in terms of modular forms. Our approach works for any modular curve; to demonstrate its efficiency, we implement our method for nonsplit Cartan modular curves.

papers.title: Asymptotically optimal degree for the double Hall property
papers.abstract: The minimum maximum degree for the double Hall property is asymptotic to sqrt(2 n). Deterministic balanced regular bipartite constructions attain this leading constant with the property on both shores and degree at most sqrt(2 n)+O(n^(21/80)) for every sufficiently large n. The construction repairs homology semibiplanes, pads by matched duplication, and completes to regularity. The all-order error term invokes the published Baker-Harman-Pintz prime-interval theorem; the formal transfer keeps that input as an explicit hypothesis.

papers.title: Asymptotics of local height pairing without Hodge conjecture
papers.abstract: We remove the assumption of the Hodge conjecture from the asymptotic formula for the Archimedean local height established in our previous work. We also remove other minor assumptions. We achieve this by exploiting the cohomological nature of Beilinson's local intersection index rather than arguing motivically.

papers.title: Ax-Schanuel with derivatives for mixed period mappings
papers.abstract: We prove the Ax-Schanuel property of the derivatives of mixed period mappings. We also prove the jet space reformulation of this result. The proofs use the Ax-Schanuel result for principal bundles with flat connections obtained by Bl\'{a}zquez-Sanz, Casale, Freitag, and Nagloo.

papers.title: Cluster scattering diagrams of acyclic affine type
papers.abstract: We give an explicit construction of the cluster scattering diagram for any acyclic exchange matrix of affine type. We show that the corresponding cluster scattering fan coincides both with the mutation fan and with a fan constructed in the almost-positive roots model.

papers.title: Cohomology of integral structure sheaves for open varieties
papers.abstract: We study the cohomology of integral structure sheaves for two types of open rigid analytic varieties: complements of divisors in quasi-compact varieties, and partially proper spaces. As applications, we prove a strengthened form of the Hebbarkeitssatz (Riemann's extension theorem), involving the almost vanishing of $R^1\lim$, and study pro-\'etale $G$-torsors on open varieties.

papers.title: Counting stringy points on a family of character varieties
papers.abstract: We provide explicit formulas for the number of stringy points over finite fields of parabolic type A character varieties with generic semisimple monodromy. This leads to formulas for their stringy E-polynomials. In particular, they satisfy the Betti Topological Mirror Symmetry Conjecture of T. Hausel and M. Thaddeus and a refinement regarding isotypic components. Our proof is based on a Frobenius-type formula for Clifford-type settings and an analysis of it in a specific set-up related to regular wreath products with cyclic groups.

papers.title: Cross-Energy of Dirichlet Partial Sums. Part 9: Zeros of the prime zeta function in its half-plane of absolute convergence
papers.abstract: The prime zeta function P(s) = ∑ₚ p⁻ˢ has zeros in its half-plane of absolute convergence. Belovas, Čepaitytė and Sabaliauskas proved that P(s) ≠ 0 for Re(s) > σₚ = 1.7795446535…, where σₚ solves P(σ) = 2¹⁻σ. We show that this bound is sharp: the closure of the real parts of the zeros in Re(s) > 1 is exactly [1, σₚ]. There are no zeros on Re(s) = σₚ, while zeros occur arbitrarily close to every line Re(s) = σ with 1 < σ < σₚ (Bohr’s method). By Jessen’s theorem, the density of real parts is J″(σ)/(2π), where J(σ) = −σ log 2 + 𝔼[log⁺(2^σ |Yσ|)], Yσ = ∑ₚ≥₃ p⁻σ eⁱθₚ, and the phases θₚ are independent and uniformly distributed. The function J is smooth, σₚ = inf{σ : J(σ) + σ log 2 = 0}, and the density vanishes at σₚ faster than any power. The argument principle, implemented with ball arithmetic, certifies exactly 68 zeros with 1.1 ≤ Re(s) ≤ 1.85 below height 2000 (70.0 predicted), and 12 zeros with Re(s) ≥ 1.5 below height 5000 (12.0 predicted). A heuristic large-deviation extrapolation predicts zeros with real part above 1.7 approximately once every 6 × 10⁶ units of height. In ½ < Re(s) < 1, P is single-valued on the half-plane with (½, 1] removed if and only if the Riemann hypothesis holds (a reformulation of a classical equivalence). Its zeros are canonical below height 3 × 10¹² and solve ζ(s) = exp(A(s)), A(s) = ∑ₘ≥₂ P(ms)/m, with |P(s)| < 2π. Below height 600, their counts for Re(s) ≥ 0.7 agree numerically with the random model. The zeros arise from cancellations between 2⁻ˢ and the contributions of the remaining primes, the prime-sum analogue of Euler-product interference behind the off-line zeros of the Davenport–Heilbronn function. We do not prove the Riemann hypothesis.

papers.title: Denominators of Hodge integrals and Minkowski numbers
papers.abstract:
We prove that the least common denominator of all genus $g$ Hodge integrals is the Minkowski number $T_{2g}$ or, equivalently, the Bhargava factorial $(2g+1)!_{\mathbb{P}}$ associated to the set of primes $\mathbb{P}\subset\mathbb{N}$. As a corollary, we prove a conjecture of Liu-Xu on the multiplicity of $3$ in the least common denominators of certain descendant integrals, and generalise their result on a conjecture of Itzykson-Zuber to Hodge integrals with $\lambda$ classes. Namely, the order of the automorphism group of any pointed stable curve of genus $g'\le g$ divides the least common denominator of all genus $g$ Hodge integrals.
  We also comment on the use of generative AI via IMProofBench, which played a fruitful part in the development of this (entirely human-written) paper.

papers.title: Densest packings of two translates of a lattice in five dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove that no packing of unit balls in $\R^5$ whose centres form two translates of a lattice is denser than the $D_5$ lattice packing. Up to congruence exactly three such packings attain this density: $\sqrt2\,D_5$, a layered packing of Leech, and the packing with Szöllősi's kissing configuration.

papers.title: Distinct partial products in prime dihedral groups
papers.abstract: Let $D_{2p}$ be the dihedral group of order $2p$, where $p$ is prime. For every fixed $0<\alpha<1$, we prove that every subset $A\subseteq D_{2p}\setminus\{e\}$ with $C_\alpha\le |A|\le p^\alpha$ admits an ordering whose nonempty partial products are pairwise distinct. Combined with the known small- and large-set theorems, this covers every subset size for all sufficiently large primes. Pairing reflections reduces the products to partial sums with fixed parity-labelled offsets. Two passes of block rotations remove distant collisions; bounded displacement allows the local condition to exclude the remaining collisions. The existence of suitable rotations follows from Pham--Sauermann's subset-sum anticoncentration theorem, an affine-rank estimate, and a count of clustered collision witnesses.

papers.title: Drinfeld presentation of affine iquantum groups via iHopf algebras
papers.abstract: Affine quantum groups $\widetilde{\mathbf{U}}$ and affine iquantum groups $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$ admit two complementary descriptions: a Serre-type presentation and a Drinfeld (current) presentation. While iquantum groups $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$ are typically defined via the Serre presentation, their Drinfeld presentations are substantially more subtle and less well understood. In this paper, we give a conceptual derivation of the Drinfeld presentation of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$ starting directly from the Drinfeld presentation of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}$, working within the framework of iHopf algebras. This approach leads naturally to the definition of iquantum affinization associated with arbitrary Kac-Moody algebras $\mathfrak{g}$. We further show that, in this general setting, these iquantum affinizations can be realized as coideal subalgebras of quantum affinizations with respect to the Drinfeld coproduct. Finally, in the affine case, we describe the imaginary root vectors $\Theta_{i,r}$ of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$ explicitly in terms of the root vectors $\psi^\pm_{i,r}$ of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}$, thereby extending the results of Li and Prze\'zdziecki for certain affine types of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$.

papers.title: Even-intersecting families of lattice paths and the Catalan numbers
papers.abstract: Shankar proved that a family of North--East lattice paths from $(0,0)$ to $(n,n)$ in which any two paths share an even number of edges has at most $2^n$ members, and conjectured that exactly $C_n$ families attain this bound, where $C_n$ is the $n$th Catalan number. We prove the conjecture. The proof determines all equality cases of the inequality behind Shankar's bound: they correspond to noncrossing partial matchings of $\{1,\dots,m\}$ whose unmatched points lie under no arc, and there are $\binom{m}{\lfloor m/2\rfloor}$ of them.

papers.title: Exact Archimedean Flicker--Rallis Periods on Cohomological Minimal $K$-Types
papers.abstract: For the symmetric pair $(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb C),\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb R))$, we compute the exact Flicker--Rallis period of a distinguished vector in a cohomological minimal $U(n)$-type, normalized by the Gel'fand--Tsetlin pairing of Hara--Miyazaki--Namikawa. Our main tool is a weight-independent identity between the Whittaker period and a compact $O(n)$-average. We determine the proportionality constant using the archimedean newform formula of Humphries--Jo, and evaluate the compact functional on the normalized distinguished vector. This yields an explicit formula for the Flicker--Rallis period for every cohomological weight.

papers.title: Exceptional zeros of Hecke $L$-functions
papers.abstract: We prove that Hecke $L$-functions have no exceptional zeros. We do so by generalising a variant due to Kerr of the proof by OpenAI in the case of Dirichlet $L$-functions.

papers.title: Explicit onsets, rates and the tail of the collision constant for heat-evolved Weyl polynomials
papers.abstract: Let $h_k$ be the orthonormal Hermite polynomials for the standard Gaussian weight, and let $a(w)=\sum_{j\ge0}a_jw^j$ be a real power series with radius of convergence greater than $1$, $a(0)\ne0$, no zeros on the unit circle and only simple zeros in the unit disk. For all large $n$ the polynomial $\sum_{j=0}^{n}a_jh_{n-j}$ has exactly as many nonreal zeros as $a$ has in the disk, but the known proof gives the onset by compactness. We make it explicit: if $a$ has no zeros in $\{1-d\le|w|\le1\}$, with $d$ below an explicit threshold, the count is exact as soon as $n$ exceeds a polynomial in $1/d$ and in the inverses of $|a(0)|$, $\min_{|w|=1}|a|$, $\min_{|w|=1-d}|a|$ and $\min_{[-1+d,1-d]}\max(|a|,|a'|)$; no separation of the nonreal zeros of $a$ is needed. By an exact identity this applies to the random Weyl polynomials $G_n$ with independent standard Gaussian coefficients under the backward heat flow $G_{n,t}=\exp(-\frac t{2n}\partial_z^2)G_n$, whose real-rooting time converges in distribution to $T_*=R_*^{-2}$, where $R_*$ is the smallest modulus of a nonreal zero of the Gaussian power series $q(w)=\sum_j\eta_jw^j$. We show that the convergence holds with the rate $n^{-\alpha}$ on $[1+\varepsilon,\infty)$ for every $\alpha<\frac3{50}$, an exponent that does not depend on $\varepsilon$; the dependence on $\varepsilon$ is removed by a super-exponential tail for the number of zeros of $q$ in a disk. Under a coupling of the degrees that shares the top coefficients, the real-rooting time $\Lambda_n$ satisfies $|\Lambda_n-T_*|\le K/n$ for $n\ge n_0$, with $K$ and $n_0$ depending on $q$. We bound $K$ and $n_0$ by polynomials in condition parameters of $q$, with absolute degrees and, when $T_*\ge1+\varepsilon$, coefficients polynomial in $1/\varepsilon$. For the Gaussian power series this gives, on the event $\{T_*\ge1+\varepsilon\}$, a power tail with exponent $1/900$ for the largest scaled displacement $D$ of the final collision of zeros, and without restriction the tail bound $\exp(-c(\log x/\log\log x)^{1/2})$; the inputs include closed forms of the two-point correlation functions of the zeros of $q$.

papers.title: Faster-than-power-law decay of order parameter correlations in the two-dimensional RP2 model: a rigorous result by vibe-proving
papers.abstract: We consider the $RP^2$ model on the two-dimensional square lattice with nearest-neighbor interactions. It is obtained by replacing the spin in the standard classical Heisenberg model with a director, which does not distinguish two opposite directions. Unlike the standard classical Heisenberg model or the O(3) nonlinear sigma model, the $RP^2$ (and its cousin $RP^3$) model allows point vortex defects classified by $\pi_1(RP^2)=Z_2$ in two dimensions. It is tempting to expect the $Z_2$ vortices to induce a phase transition analogous to the well-established Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition in the O(2) model (XY model) in two dimensions. Indeed, the possibilities of a critical phase or a critical point with power-law correlations of the order parameter in the $RP^2$ and $RP^3$ models have been discussed in the literature. However, the challenging nature of the problem has prevented a definitive conclusion on the phase diagram so far. In this paper, we report a rigorous mathematical proof by Artificial Intelligence (ChatGPT 6 Astra) that the absolute value of the two-point correlation function of order parameters at distance $r$ in the $RP^2$ and $RP^3$ models on the two-dimensional square lattice is bounded above by $C_\beta \exp\{-c_\beta[\log(2+r)]^2\}$ for any finite inverse temperature $\beta\ge0$, with positive constants $C_\beta$ and $c_\beta$ depending only on $\beta$. Namely, the correlation function decays faster than any power of $r$. The proof is formalized and verified in Lean; the formalization is publicly available at \href{https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23548847}{doi:10.5281/zenodo.23548847}. A heuristic argument based on a one-parameter effective theory ansatz at large distances combined with the rigorous correlation bound suggests (but does not prove) that the $Z_2$ vortices are always unbound at any nonzero temperature.

papers.title: Finiteness of Planar Central Configurations for Five Positive Masses
papers.abstract: We prove that, for any five positive masses, there are finitely many planar Newtonian central configurations up to translations, rotations, and positive scaling. Building on the singular-diagram framework of Albouy and Kaloshin, we treat the exceptional masses left open by their finiteness theorem. The proof retains a lower bound for the physical potential after passing to the complex algebraic equations. On each fixed potential level, energy estimates, torque identities, and local response calculations control the possible degenerations. A polynomial selection argument then yields finiteness. The exceptional local calculations and their algebraic certificates are given explicitly. A separate Lean development accompanies the proof.

papers.title: Formal models for relative adic spaces
papers.abstract: We extend Raynaud's theory of formal models from rigid-analytic spaces over a nonarchimedean field to uniform qcqs adic spaces $X$, with no finite-type assumptions, over an arbitrary Tate affinoid base $S$. The key new ingredient is the notion of a normalized formal blow-up which takes on the role played by admissible formal blow-ups in the classical theory.

papers.title: Gamma conjectures for Milnor hypersurfaces
papers.abstract:
We prove Gamma conjectures I and II of Galkin, Golyshev and Iritani for Milnor hypersurfaces, the smooth hypersurfaces of bidegree $(1,1)$ in the product of two projective spaces.
  We provide a criterion for Gamma conjecture II for general Fano manifolds, generalizing the criterion by Hu and Ke. Using the mirror symmetry technique of Galkin and Iritani, we establish global Gamma-I for Milnor hypersurfaces, thereby proving Gamma conjecture I as a special case. Using it, together with the Galois action and our criterion, we verify Gamma conjecture II for Milnor hypersurfaces.

papers.title: Gluing defects for projected coarse graining in finite spin-foam models
papers.abstract: Orthogonal truncation can discard states that contribute to a later boundary amplitude. For a self-adjoint contraction $T$ on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space and an isometric inclusion $s$ of retained states, we prove that the two-step residual $\Delta=s^*T^2s-(s^*Ts)^2$ controls every finite placement of intermediate projections in every Schatten norm. For blocks of lengths $n_1,\ldots,n_k$, the error is at most $\sum_{i<j}n_in_j\|\Delta\|$, and the constant is optimal even for positive contractions. The residual vanishes exactly when the retained subspace is invariant. Two-dimensional finite-group gauge sums realize an idempotent projected transfer operator with nonzero residual, as well as positive-semidefinite transfer operators with identical one-step retained data and different residuals. We derive their gluing and subdivision identities with explicit boundary measures and BF normalization. We also bound the accumulation of local errors under tensor contraction and the distance to compatible linear amplitude data. Colimits extend compatible amplitude families, and quotients by invariant subspaces preserve the comparison maps. A measurement map that is injective on the retained ansatz gives a unique normalized least-squares fit. Exact rational calculations reproduce the finite-group examples and the blocking comparisons.

papers.title: Langlands-Shahidi gamma factors and local transfer in families
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a quasi-split $p$-adic group, defined over a non-archimedean local field of residue cardinality $q$, and $R$ be a $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{q}^{-1},\mu_{4p^\infty}]$-algebra. We generalize the constructions of Shahidi local coefficients and Langlands-Shahidi gamma factors to the setting of co-Whittaker $R$-representations. For classical $p$-adic groups, we prove there is a unique integral morphism of endomorphism rings of Gelfand--Graev representations, interpolating the (standard) local generic transfer to a general linear group. This yields a local transfer morphism in families, which allows us to deduce properties of the local $\ell$-adic generic transfer and congruences modulo primes $\ell\neq p$.

papers.title: Leafrians, Poisson structures, and Frobenius splittings on moduli spaces
papers.abstract: The Poisson $T$-Pfaffians of Bott--Samelson varieties, $G/U$, and $G/B$ produce Frobenius splittings, but only by a local, coordinate-bound argument. We isolate the local mechanism: a weighted trace pairing on the deformation space of a fat point, whose top coefficient factors over the blocks. At the members of a presentation, polyvector fields on the base $X$ transfer to the moduli space $M$. Applied to a Poisson bivector, this produces a Poisson bivector, extending Bottacin's structure from surfaces to arbitrary dimension. Applied to a top degree polyvector $s$ and wedged with a transverse Euler frame, it produces an anticanonical section on $M$, which we call the \emph{leafrian}. When $X$ is a Poisson surface, we prove that the leafrian splits the moduli of stable sheaves, of principal $G$-bundles, and of instantons if and only if $s$ Frobenius-splits the base. The mechanism itself is dimension-free. The construction also recovers and generalizes the splittings of the Lie-theoretic examples: the $r$-matrix need not satisfy the classical Yang--Baxter equation.

papers.title: Lehmer's totient problem with fewer than sixteen prime factors
papers.abstract: A composite number $n$ whose totient divides $n-1$ was known to have at least fourteen prime factors. We prove that it has at least sixteen, at least $16001$ if $(n-1)/\varphi(n)\ge3$, and more than $10^8$ if $3\mid n$, and that $n<2^{2^{k-7}}$ if $n$ has $k$ prime factors. For the companion equation $\varphi(n)\mid n+1$ we show that the nine known solutions are the only ones with at most eight prime factors, and that a further solution prime to $3$ has at least sixteen. Each statement is reduced by hand to a finite computation, which independent programs carry out. Lehmer's conjecture remains open, and we state the assertion that would settle it.

papers.title: Linear systems on blow-ups of Hirzebruch surfaces
papers.abstract: Motivated by various equivalent versions of the SHGH conjecture for $\mathbb P^2$ blown up at very general points, we propose a similar conjecture for Hirzebruch surfaces. We prove that this conjecture is true for the Hirzebruch surface $\mathbb F_e$ blown up at $r\leqslant e+5$ very general points.

papers.title: Local heights for nef toric compactified divisors
papers.abstract: We present a definition of a local height of nef toric divisors in the sense of Yuan and Zhang by approximating a height for canonical divisors and then using the local energy to extend to other metrics on the same geometric divisor.

papers.title: Log blow-ups and global resolutions in rigid geometry
papers.abstract: In this article, we study log blow-ups in the setting of log adic spaces. As in the theory of log schemes, we prove the existence of global resolutions of toric singularities for fs log adic spaces log smooth over a $p$-adic field, and the acyclicity of certain sheaves under log blow-ups. One new feature of (log) rigid analytic varieties is their integral structure sheaf: we prove that it is also almost acyclic under log blow-ups in the Kummer \'etale topology. We also supply some foundational results on log adic spaces.

papers.title: Nilpotent-free spaces of 3 x 3 matrices over the field with three elements
papers.abstract: Wigderson conjectured that for every finite field $F$ and every $n\ge1$ there is a space of $n\times n$ matrices over $F$ of dimension $n^2-\binom n2$ whose only nilpotent element is zero. We show that every six-dimensional space of $3\times3$ matrices over $\F_3$ contains a nonzero nilpotent matrix, so the conjecture fails for $F=\F_3$ and $n=3$; the largest possible dimension is five.

papers.title: Non-Archimedean Smale Mean Value and Dubinin–Sugawa Dual Mean Value Problems
papers.abstract: Motivated by the Smale mean value and the Dubinin–Sugawa dual mean value theorems, we formulate non-Archimedean Smale mean value and Dubinin–Sugawa dual mean value problems. We show that if a universal constant satisfying the non-Archimedean Smale mean value problem exists, it must be greater than or equal to one and if a universal constant satisfying the non-Archimedean Dubinin–Sugawa dual mean value problem exists, it must be less than or equal to one. We also derive other bounds whenever roots of unity exist in a non-Archimedean field.

papers.title: Nonexistence of lim Cohen–Macaulay modules following [Che26] and [Ang26]
papers.abstract: Using the inequality stated in [ Che26, Main Claim 1.1], we prove nonexistence of lim Cohen–Macaulay sequences for the completed section rings of smooth projective surfaces over C with an ample globally generated divisor H satisfying KY ≡ 4H and 15H2/8 > χ(OY ). Such a pair is exhibited in [Ang26, Corollary 4.3], with H2 = 1080 and χ(OY ) = 1926. For a complete local domain (R, m) with ℓRHj m(R) < ∞ for 0 ≤ j < dim R, we prove that a lim Cohen–Macaulay sequence in the sense of Bhatt, Hochster, and Ma [ BHM26 ] exists if and only if a lim Γm-Cohen–Macaulay sequence exists (Definition 1.1). These may be different sequences. Chen’s geometric inequality [Che26, Main Claim 1.1] obstructs lim Γm-Cohen–Macaulay sequences over the completed section rings above. The comparison therefore rules out lim Cohen–Macaulay sequences over those rings.

papers.title: Obstructions to deforming space curves lying on a complete intersection of quadrics
papers.abstract: Let $S=S_{2,\ldots,2}\subset\mathbb P^{n+2}$ be a smooth complete intersection of $n$ quadrics containing a line $E$, where $n\geq 3$, and set $D=(n-1)\mathbf h+E$, where $\mathbf h=[\mathcal O_S(1)]$. We study the deformations of smooth curves $C\in |mD|$ and their obstructions. The linear system $|D|$ defines a birational morphism $f:S\to\overline S$ that contracts $E$ to a point and realizes an unprojection in the sense of Papadakis--Reid. When $n=3$, the surface $S=S_{2,2,2}\subset\mathbb P^5$ is a $K3$ surface and $E$ is a $(-2)$-curve. We prove that the complementary open surface $S\setminus E$ admits first-order infinitesimal deformations in $\mathbb P^5\setminus E$ that are obstructed at the second order. Using these obstructions, we show that, for every sufficiently large $m$ with $\operatorname{char} k\nmid m$, there exists a generically non-reduced irreducible component $W_m$ of the Hilbert scheme $\operatorname{Hilb}^{sc}\mathbb P^5$ of smooth connected curves in $\mathbb P^5$. Its general member $C$ lies on a complete intersection $S_{2,2,2}$ of three quadrics, satisfies $C\sim mD$, and has $h^0(N_{C/\mathbb P^5})-\dim_{[C]}\operatorname{Hilb}^{sc}\mathbb P^5=3$. In contrast, when $n>3$, we prove that, for every sufficiently large $m$ with $\operatorname{char} k\nmid m$, the corresponding family of curves in $|mD|$ gives rise to a generically smooth irreducible component of $\operatorname{Hilb}^{sc}\mathbb P^{n+2}$.

papers.title: On Automorphism Groups of (1,2)-Surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a minimal surface of general type with $K_S^2=1$ and $p_g(S)=2$, called a $(1,2)$-surface. We give a geometric recovery and refinement of D. Wen's bound $|\mathrm{Aut}(S)|\leq 200$ using the canonical genus-two fibration and the double-cover model over the Hirzebruch surface $\Sigma_2$. Computing $\mathrm{Aut}(\Sigma_2)$ from its Cox ring separates the action on the base $\mathbb{P}^1$ from the vertical kernel. If $\overline K_0$ denotes the vertical image on $\Sigma_2$, then $\overline K_0$ is cyclic of order $5$, $4$, $2$, or $1$, and we prove the respective sharp bounds $|\mathrm{Aut}(S)|\leq 200, 192, 48, 80$. The proof combines singularity indices of genus-two fibrations with invariant divisors arising from the branch equation. We also construct admissible branch divisors attaining all four bounds and show that their full automorphism groups are, respectively, $(C_{10}\times C_{10})\rtimes C_2$, $(BO_{48}\times C_8)/\langle(-I,J^4)\rangle$, $(BT_{24}\times C_4)/\langle(-I,J^2)\rangle$, and $C_{40}\times C_2$. Here $BO_{48}$ and $BT_{24}$ denote the binary octahedral and binary tetrahedral groups, respectively, and $J$ denotes a generator of the corresponding cyclic factor.

papers.title: On Borodin-Gorin presentation of Heckman-Opdam $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ hypergeometric function
papers.abstract: We prove that Borodin-Gorin presentation for Heckman-Opdam $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ hypergeometric function by interlacing integrals is equivalent to two other integral presentations studied in arXiv:2508.18864. We also consider related Baxter operators and the corresponding limiting procedure from the Ruijsenaars hyperbolic model.

papers.title: On invariant $1$-dimensional representations of a finite $W$-algebra
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a simple Lie algebra over $\mathbf{C}$ and $G$ be the corresponding simply connected algebraic group. Consider a nilpotent element $e\in \mathfrak{g}$, the corresponding element $\chi=(e, \bullet)$ in $\mathfrak{g}^*$, and the coadjoint orbit $\mathbf{O}=G\chi$. We are interested in the set $\mathfrak{J}\mathfrak{d}^1(\mathcal{W})$ of codimension $1$ ideals $J\subset \mathcal{W}$ in a finite $W$-algebra $\mathcal{W}=U(\mathfrak{g}, e)$. We have a natural action of the component group $\Gamma=Z_G(\chi)/Z_G^\circ(\chi)$ on $\mathfrak{J}\mathfrak{d}^1(\mathcal{W})$. Denote the set of $\Gamma$-stable points of $\mathfrak{J}\mathfrak{d}^1(\mathcal{W})$ by $\mathfrak{J}\mathfrak{d}^{1}(\mathcal{W})^{\Gamma}$. For a classical $\mathfrak{g}$ Premet and Topley proved that $\mathfrak{J}\mathfrak{d}^{1}(\mathcal{W})^{\Gamma}$ are parameterized by the points of an affine space. In this paper we will give an alternative proof of this fact using completely different approach. As a corollary of our construction, we imply that for classical $\mathfrak{g}$ all $\Gamma$-invariant $1$-dimensional representations of $\mathcal{W}$ are obtained by a parabolic induction introduced by Losev.

papers.title: On orbits of the automorphism group of toroidal spherical varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the orbits of the automorphism group on a toroidal spherical variety. In the affine case, we prove that two points lie in the same orbit of the identity component if and only if the kernels of the homomorphisms from the divisor class group to their local divisor class groups coincide. These kernels are described in terms of $B$-stable prime divisors. For a smooth complete toroidal spherical variety, we obtain a similar criterion using the monoids generated by the classes of $B$-stable prime divisors that do not contain a given $G$-orbit.

papers.title: On Stanley-Reisner Rings with Minimal Betti Numbers
papers.abstract: We study simplicial complexes with a given number of vertices whose Stanley-Reisner ring has the minimal sum of Betti numbers. We prove that every full subcomplex of them is homotopy equivalent either to a point or to a sphere. Moreover, we prove that such kind of simplicial complexes coincide with those having minimal Taylor resolutions.

papers.title: On the $\theta$-split side of the local relative trace formula
papers.abstract: The author derives an expression for one side of the local relative trace formula, at the level of Lie algebras, by combining methods of Arthur and Harish-Chandra with the structure theory for reductive symmetric spaces.

papers.title: On the Kummer pro-\'etale cohomology of $\mathbb B_{\operatorname{dR}}$
papers.abstract: We investigate $p$-adic cohomologies of log rigid analytic varieties over a $p$-adic field. For a log rigid analytic variety $X$ defined over a discretely valued field, we compute the Kummer pro-\'etale cohomology of $\mathbb{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^+$ and $\mathbb{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}$. When $X$ is defined over $\mathbb{C}_p$, we introduce a logarithmic ${B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^+$-cohomology theory, serving as a deformation of log de Rham cohomology. Additionally, we establish the log de Rham-\'etale comparison in this setting and prove the degeneration of both the Hodge-Tate and Hodge-log de Rham spectral sequences when $X$ is proper and log smooth.

papers.title: On The Motivic Leray-Hirsch Theorem For Pure Tate Fibre Bundles
papers.abstract: We prove a Leray-Hirsch theorem for a smooth proper morphism over a smooth integral base whose generic fibre has a pure Tate motive. We further explore and highlight some key applications of this theorem.

papers.title: On the rational points in conics of a cubic surface
papers.abstract: We study rational and integral points lying on finite collections of conics on non-ruled cubic surfaces over a number field. We extend the global determinant method to hypersurfaces in linear subvarieties, retaining dependence on the height of their Cayley forms. The universal Deligne pairing identifies the Chow line bundle on a residual conic pencil with three times of the universal bundle. Uniform bounds for cubic curves then control the number of conics of bounded height and give uniform estimates for their contribution to auxiliary coverings.

papers.title: On The Rational Realization of Even-dimensional Spheres and Products of Eilenberg--MacLane Spaces as Classifying Spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the rational realization problem for the classifying space $B\mathrm{aut}_1(X)$. We prove that if $S^{2n}$ is realized as $B\mathrm{aut}_1(X)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ for a simply-connected space $X$, then $X$ is $\pi$-infinite and has vanishing rational Gottlieb elements above degree $2n-1$. In particular, even-dimensional spheres cannot be realized as $B\mathrm{aut}_1(X)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ for any simply-connected $\pi$-finite space $X$. We also prove that, for all $n\geq 2$ and $s,t\geq 1$, the product of Eilenberg--MacLane spaces $K(\mathbb{Q}^s,n)\times K(\mathbb{Q}^t,n+1)$ cannot be realized as $B\mathrm{aut}_1(X)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ for any simply-connected $\pi$-finite space $X$. Moreover, we prove that if $r\geq 2$, $n\geq 3$ and $K(\mathbb{Q}^r,n)$ is realized as $B\mathrm{aut}_1(X)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ for a simply-connected $\pi$-finite space $X$, then $X$ has the rational homotopy type of $K(\mathbb{Q}^r,n-1)$. The proofs are based on two structural results for Gottlieb elements in the derivation Lie algebra of a Sullivan minimal model, which provide a uniform method for these realization problems.

papers.title: On the transcendental Yau-Tian-Donaldson Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the (uniform) Yau-Tian-Donaldson Conjecture for transcendental K\"ahler classes in the case of trivial automorphisms. Indeed, we show the existence of Special K\"ahler Fujita Approximations of big cohomology classes associated to big test configurations, establishing the equivalence between the uniform $K$-stability and the strengthened version for models. More generally, we show that any big cohomology class on a compact K\"ahler manifold admits such Special K\"ahler Fujita Approximations: the volume and the analogue of the Riemann-Roch coefficient of the big class are both approximated by those of K\"ahler classes on higher compactifications.

papers.title: Origin-Centered Möbius Circles and Dyadic Pairings of the Riemann Zeta Function on the Critical Line
papers.abstract: We investigate the complex geometry of the normalized Dirichlet eta terms tn(s) = 1 1−2 1−s (−1)n−1 ns (s = a + bi). By analyzing the Möbius geometry of each term, we demonstrate that the base-2 resonant partial sum S2(s) = t1(s) + t2(s) forms an exact circle. Remarkably, this base circle is centered strictly at the origin (0, 0) if and only if Re(s) = 1 2 . We further establish a dyadic pairing theorem showing that every oddeven pair Pm(s) = tm(s) + t2m(s) inherits this origin-centered circular symmetry on the critical line. Analyzing the phase distribution on these concentric circles reveals four geometric mechanisms that distinguish non-trivial Riemann zeta zeros b = bn from generic values of b, including right-half-plane slow-zone clustering of P1 and opposinghemisphere alignment of the leading inner circles P3, P5, P7. Finally, we prove that removing all odd-even dyadic pairs leaves the multiples-of-4 subseries P∞ k=1 t4k(s) = t4(s)ζ(s), whose partial sums spiral around a target center Ctarget(b) that coincides with the origin (0, 0) if and only if b is a Riemann zeta zero.

papers.title: Plabic promotions beyond cluster: quantum cluster structures and the dual canonical basis
papers.abstract: Plabic tangles define geometric promotion maps between configurations and, after choosing a lift, between Grassmannians. The main conjecture in \cite{Tangles} is that when the tangle is dominant and solvable the induced algebraic promotion is cluster quasi-homomorphism. This work extends the cluster perspective in two directions. First, we initiate the study of quantum promotions. We conjecture that all promotions defined from dominant solvable tangles are naturally lifted to a \emph{quantum cluster quasi homomorphism}, and prove for all cases in the literature that the were shown to be (classical) cluster quasi-homomorphisms. Secondly, we define the notion of cluster-Lusztig quasi-homomorphisms, which are cluster quasi homomorphisms that take Lustig's dual canonical basis elements to dual canonical basis element, up to a Laurent monomial in frozen variables, with clearing and normalization chosen uniformly on each content component. We prove the unexpected result that the classical and quantum $m$-unary star promotions fall into this category, and conjecture that all promotions coming from dominant solvable tangles share the same property. We then consider promotions via non solvable cores of intersection number higher than one. We use it to study facets of amplituhedron cells, and to show that some of them do not lie in zero loci of dual canonical basis elements, disproving a conjecture by T. Lam \cite{LamGP}.

papers.title: Point Separation for Adjoint Line Bundles
papers.abstract: Let X be a smooth complex projective variety of dimension n and let L be an ample line bundle. Using the freeness and minimization inputs specified in the introduction, we prove that KX + mL separates distinct points for every integer m ≥ n + 2, the sharp bound predicted by Fujita’s very ampleness conjecture. Exponential-moment convergence produces point-centred minimizing valuations at both points in a common degree. Strict convexity then gives a divisor with discrepancy equality at one point and strict excess at the other. A rational perturbation on a resolution, followed by Kawamata–Viehweg vanishing and descent, gives the required sections

papers.title: Positivity of supercritical LYZ pairs
papers.abstract: We introduce the roots of supercritical Leung--Yau--Zaslow pairs and prove pointwise strong positivity of the associated Schur forms. The resulting LYZ cones contain the pliant cone on smooth projective threefolds, with strict inclusion on a Fujino--Sato threefold. We also establish Hard Lefschetz and Hodge--Riemann relations for the associated Chern classes on compact K\"ahler manifolds in bidegrees $1\le p+q\le\dim X$ with $\min\{p,q\}\le1$.

papers.title: Projective-plane determinant bounds for sparse binary matrices
papers.abstract: For every integer density r from 3 through 14, a binary square matrix with e ones satisfies an explicit affine-exponential determinant bound. Under e <= r n this gives the projective-plane determinant rate, with equality precisely for direct sums of projective-plane incidence matrices of order r-1. Individual row and column degrees are unrestricted. The written proof uses an exact finite scalar certificate with rigorous unbounded-degree tails; the companion contains a pinned 98-module Lean mathematics closure.

papers.title: Properties of theories whose algebras are free
papers.abstract: A hard theorem of Givant classifies the finitary algebraic theories for which every algebra is free. From it, one easily deduces that all such theories are minimal (adding any further equations makes them trivial) and have a well-defined notion of dimension (free algebras on sets of different cardinality are never isomorphic). We prove both these properties directly, without the aid of Givant's theorem.

papers.title: Quantum field theory and four-manifolds: Perspectives from physics and geometry
papers.abstract: These lecture notes are based on lecture series by the authors for the Summer School 2025 on ``Physical mathematics of quantum field theory" at the University of Massachusetts Amherst organized by Owen Gwilliam, Chris Elliott, and Matteo Lotito. The lectures centred around algebraic structures arising from twists of supersymmetric quantum field theories, correlation functions of topologically twisted supersymmetric gauge theories, and their mathematical counterparts as intersection-theoretic invariants associated to moduli spaces of instantons, semistable sheaves, or Higgs sheaves on four-manifolds or complex projective surfaces.

papers.title: Quantum K-structure constants and cylindric Grothendieck polynomials for Grassmannians
papers.abstract: We use the partition functions of a five-vertex exactly solvable lattice model from statistical mechanics to give new combinatorial formulae for the Schubert structure constants of torus-equivariant quantum K-theory rings of Grassmannians. The proofs build on our earlier results where we identified the transfer matrices of these lattice models geometrically as multiplications by the Hirzebruch $\lambda_y$ classes of the tautological subbundle and the (dual) quotient bundle. The structure constants are solutions of a system of linear equations with coefficients given by the partition function. This system may be solved explicitly by specializing the Hirzebruch parameter $y$ to an equivariant parameter, leading to explicit formulae using Cramer's rule. Furthermore, we give an alternative combinatorial construction of the partition functions in terms of sums over cylindric set-valued tableaux, which we call cylindric Grothendieck polynomials. The latter generalise McNamara's factorial skew Grothendieck and Yeliussizov's modified Grothendieck polynomials and can be thought of as an equivariant K-theoretic version of Postnikov's toric Schur function. We also provide new polynomial representatives for equivariant K-theory classes of Richardson varieties and their variants.

papers.title: Quantum theory of molecular orientation
papers.abstract: We formulate a quantum phase space for rotational and nuclear-spin states of rigid molecules. For each nuclear spin isomer, we re-derive the isomer's admissible angular momentum states from molecular geometry and nuclear-spin data, introduce its angular position states using quantization theory, and develop a generalized Fourier transform converting between the two. We classify molecules into three types -- asymmetric, rotationally symmetric, and perrotationally symmetric -- with the last type having no macroscopic analogue due to nuclear-spin statistics constraints. We discuss two general features in perrotationally symmetric state spaces that are Hamiltonian-independent and induced solely by symmetry and spin statistics. First, we quantify when and how an isomer's state space is completely rotation-spin entangled, meaning that it does not admit any separable states. Second, we identify isomers whose position states house an internal pseudo-spin or "fiber" degree of freedom, and the fiber's Berry phase or matrix after adiabatic changes in position yields naturally robust operations, akin to braiding anyonic quasiparticles or realizing fault-tolerant quantum gates. We outline how the fiber can be used as a quantum error-correcting code and discuss scenarios where these features can be experimentally probed

papers.title: Ramsey’s Theorem for Pairs in Pincus’s Model XI
papers.abstract: Howard and Rubin record Pincus’s ordered colored permutation model as N48, but do not determine whether Ramsey’s theorem for pairs holds there. We prove that N48 |= RT for pairs. The proof uses least finite supports and the homogeneity of Pincus’s ordered colored structure: after fixing all but one point of a support, the remaining point generates an infinite orbit whose unordered pairs form a single stabilizer orbit. Combining this with Pincus’s results on the dense linear ordering principle (DO), the Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem (BPI), and the failure of Part∞, together with Pincus’s transfer theorems, yields Con(ZF) ⇒ Con(ZF + RT_pairs + DO + BPI + ¬Part∞), where Part∞ states that every infinite set is the disjoint union of infinitely many infinite sets.

papers.title: Reflexive Descent to Minimal Seeds in the Kreuzer--Skarke List
papers.abstract: Kreuzer and Skarke built the list of reflexive polytopes by growing it from small seed polytopes. We ask how far a polytope can be from its seeds when it is shrunk through reflexive polytopes only, one at a time and without skipping any. Such a descent always exists and always ends at a seed. In four dimensions no descent takes more than 348 steps, which proves the conjecture of a uniform transition depth, and in two and three dimensions the exact maxima are five and eleven. In four dimensions two polytopes with thirty-seven lattice points need exactly twenty-two steps, so the maximum lies between twenty-two and 348.

papers.title: Regulator Constants and Cohomology
papers.abstract: We show how regulator constants of a finitely generated $\mathbb{Z}[G]$-module can be related to $G$-cohomology, where $G$ is a finite group. We then derive consequences of such relation for modules naturally arising in number theory, such as ring of integers and units of number fields, $K$-theory groups of ring of integers and Mordell-Weil groups of elliptic curves.

papers.title: Relative Hitchin fibrations and endoscopy for Unitary Friedberg--Jacquet varieties
papers.abstract: We prove a relative fundamental lemma for the unitary symmetric variety $GL_n(k')\backslash U_{2n}$, proving a conjecture of Leslie, Xiao, and Zhang. Our proof reduces to the Lie algebra and argues over function fields in positive characteristic, using methods from Ngo-Laumon and Ngo. In particular, we reinterpret orbital integrals in terms of the cohomology of relative affine Springer fibers and globalize this using unitary versions of Hitchin moduli spaces for symmetric pairs via a product formula. As the main global input, we prove a matching of perverse sheaves between relative Hitchin moduli spaces and their corresponding endoscopic variants.

papers.title: Representations of Coxeter groups over fusion rings and hyperplane complements
papers.abstract: We study faithful realisations of Coxeter groups over fusion rings and study Vinberg systems associated to them. We show that they induce embeddings of hyperplane complements, which provide geometrical realisations of certain types of strong admissible (LCM) homomorphisms between Artin--Tits groups.

papers.title: Restricted (2+1)-TQFTs supported by thickened and solid tori
papers.abstract: A faithful $(1+1)$ TQFT has recently been constructed, but the existence of a faithful $(2+1)$ TQFT remains an open question, that subsumes the hard problem of linearity of mapping class groups of surfaces. To circumvent the latter problem we construct a subcategory of the category of 3-cobordisms, containing disjoint unions of tori and simplest cobordisms between them. On this we define TQFTs that are able to distinguish pairs of torus bundles and lens spaces, previously shown not to be distinguishable by quantum invariants.

papers.title: Rigid and $\tau$-locally free modules via Taft algebras
papers.abstract: We show that rigid modules are $\tau$-locally free for a large family of 1-Iwanaga--Gorenstein algebras. This family includes many cases of the algebras introduced by Geiss--Leclerc--Schr\"oer in their Inventiones paper "Quivers with relations for symmetrizable Cartan matrices I: Foundations", hence answering a question posed by Geiss--Leclerc--Schr\"oer for many new cases. Our result is achieved by introducing coactions of Taft algebras and applying the recent theory developed by the first-named author and Coulembier.

papers.title: Rigidity, flexibility, and a sign error
papers.abstract: The documents [OAI26a, OAI26b, OAI26c] claimed to prove cases of the Hodge conjecture via homological mirror symmetry, before being withdrawn by OpenAI. We discuss the source of the error (but do not analyse the rest of the argument).

papers.title: Segre determinants and MHV gravity amplitudes
papers.abstract: We describe a Segre-Veronese construction of polynomial solutions to the interpolation conditions of the numerators of tree-level MHV gravity amplitudes given by Hodges' formula. The five- and six-point Hodges numerators arise from Segre determinants, while for every $n\geq7$ suitable Segre determinants lead to solutions linearly independent of the Hodges numerator. The existence of such independent elements for $n=7,8$ was recently established by Mai and Zhang.

papers.title: Semi-infinite parabolic IC-sheaf II: the Ran space version
papers.abstract: This paper is a sequel to arXiv:2310.0638. Let G be a split reductive group. We define the parabolic semi-infinite category on the Ran version of the affine Grassmanian Gr_{G,Ran}. We study the semi-infinite parabolic IC-sheaf in this category. We provide several descriptions of this object, one as certain colimit, another as an intermediate extension in certain category. We relate the global and local semi-infinite categories of sheaves. We also relate the intersection cohomology sheaf of the Drinfeld compactification of Bun_P with the semi-infinite parabolic IC-sheaf.

papers.title: Semi-strict 4-categories as enriched categories
papers.abstract: We introduce several flavours of semi-strict 4-category as enriched categories. We give the axioms for semi-strict 4-categories in elementary terms and describe a wide range of examples. In particular, we answer the question of what exactly Gray-categories and the higher transformations between them form: namely, a left-sharp 4-category G-Cat$^4$. In addition, we describe examples arising from braided monoidal 2-categories, monoidal Gray-categories (herein defined) and Gray-categories with structure. We use the concepts introduced here and the relationships between them to unify various concepts in the literature, such as Crans' 4-teisi. In the second part of the paper, we investigate homotopical aspects. In particular, we classify the equivalence n-cells in the left-sharp 4-category G-Cat$^4$ for each n. Using this, we show that the left-sharp skew monoidal structure on the category of Gray-categories induces a symmetric monoidal closed structure on the homotopy category of Gray-categories.

papers.title: Small algebraic integers and Frobenius prime sums
papers.abstract: The determinant argument in recent proofs of Landau–Siegel zero exclusion compares the size of a nonzero integer with its divisibility by inert primes. We observe that the same comparison applies to every Frobenius class in a finite Galois extension of $\mathbb{Q}$, bounding its weighted prime count in terms of the supply of small algebraic integers. For each fixed field, the resulting height bound implies a weighted Chebotarev theorem whose only analytic inputs are the elementary Chebyshev and Mertens estimates. In the quadratic case there are only two Frobenius classes, so the lower bound obtained by complementation remains uniform in the conductor; this recovers Landau–Siegel zero exclusion.

papers.title: Some homotopy coherent finite group actions on spheres
papers.abstract: We provide some examples of homotopy coherent smooth finite group actions on spheres which do not arise from strict actions.

papers.title: Superfluid Stiffness and Nonclassical Rotational Inertia of the Dilute Hard-Sphere Bose Gas
papers.abstract: We study the three-dimensional Bose gas of hard spheres of diameter $a$ at density $\rho$ and temperature $T$, in the thermodynamic limit with $a$, $\rho$, and $T$ fixed. When the gas parameter $\rho a^3$ is sufficiently small and $0<T<T_*$, we prove two equilibrium signatures of superfluidity. First, in a periodic box, the superfluid fraction, defined through the free-energy cost of twisted boundary conditions, has thermodynamic lower limit at least $c\,(\rho a^3)^{3/8}$, uniformly in $T$ in this interval. Second, in dilations of an arbitrary nonempty bounded open container with hard walls, the nonclassical rotational inertia fraction $1-I/I_{\mathrm{cl}}$ has thermodynamic lower limit at least $c'(\rho a^3)^{3/8}$ for every fixed rotation axis, where $I$ is the moment of inertia, $I_{\mathrm{cl}}$ its classical value, and $c'>0$ depends only on the container and the axis. In both results the derivative of the free energy is taken at finite volume, before the thermodynamic limit. The temperature $T_*$ is of order $(\rho a^3)^{1/3}/\log(1/(\rho a^3))$ times the critical temperature of the ideal Bose gas. We also bound the moment generating function of the winding vector of the Feynman–Kac paths by that of a centered Gaussian, at every density and positive temperature. Combining this upper bound with the first result, we determine the order of the winding fluctuations in the regime above. Further, for $0<\varepsilon\le1$, $\rho a^3\le(\varepsilon/100)^3$, and $T\ge(1+\varepsilon)4\pi\rho^{2/3}$, about $1.9(1+\varepsilon)$ times the critical temperature of the ideal Bose gas, the superfluid fraction in a periodic box tends to zero exponentially in its side length. By identities of Pollock and Ceperley and of Sindzingre, Klein, and Ceperley, we can express the two responses as multiples of the variances of the winding and of the signed projected area of the paths. We bound these variances from below with a variance inequality of Hammersley–Chapman–Robbins type, applied to random rewirings of the paths in a short imaginary-time interval along closed lattice routes. The rewirings adapt route comparisons developed in OpenAI's preprints on Bose–Einstein condensation in dilute Bose gases, and we extend the thermal estimates of the positive-temperature hard-sphere preprint in that series to higher temperatures. We average the rewirings over randomly translated closed lattice walks whose independent copies rarely approach each other. This makes the changed law close to the original law in chi-square divergence. Using conditional independence between disjoint imaginary-time intervals, we obtain bounds uniform in temperature. We also transfer the thermal estimates to arbitrary containers.

papers.title: Supersymmetric Yang--Mills theories with several times reduce to ten dimensions
papers.abstract: Supersymmetric Yang--Mills theories in signatures with several times are built by restricting the gaugino to the kernel of $k$ mutually orthogonal null vectors and letting the supersymmetry close on translations contracted with their product. We prove that every theory of this kind, defined by five axioms that Nishino's construction satisfies, has residual dimension $s+t-2k$ equal to ten (or to two, a degenerate case), and that its null vectors can be real only if $k\le\min(s,t)$.
