The cubic fermion terms reduce to a Fierz identity on the residual spinors, and that identity forces the dimension of the spinors to be $2(d-2)$ on a $d$-dimensional vector space, which happens only for $d=3,4,6,10$. With Majorana--Weyl spinors the signature must therefore satisfy $s-t\in\{8,0,-8\}$. There is no such theory in $(9+8n)+1$, $(10+8n)+2$, $(11+8n)+3$ or $(12+8n)+4$ for $n\ge1$, although it has been claimed that the existence proofs for the signatures $(9+m)+(1+m)$ carry over to these; the signatures $27+3$ and $19+3$ are among those excluded. For a single time the result does not depend on the construction: in $(9+8n)+1$ with $n\ge1$ every massless multiplet without tensor charges has at least $2^{2^{2+4n}}$ states, so a unitary theory with no tensor charges on its massless states has no massless vector multiplet.

papers.title: The book Ramsey number $R(B_{57},B_{58})=231$
papers.abstract: We construct a graph on $230$ vertices with no book $B_{57}$ whose complement contains no $B_{58}$. With the upper bound of Rousseau and Sheehan this gives $R(B_{57},B_{58})=231$, the smallest case of Wesley's conjecture $R(B_{n-1},B_n)=4n-1$ that was open. The graph is a two-block circulant graph over $\Z_{115}$, and the proof reduces to $57$ inequalities.

papers.title: The bridge index and the nonorientable four-genus of knots with at most thirteen crossings
papers.abstract:
We determine two invariants for knots that the KnotInfo database leaves open. KnotInfo lists the bridge index of  total{} prime knots with thirteen crossings as either $3$ or $4$; we prove that  closed{} of them have bridge index and meridional rank $4$, so the meridional rank conjecture holds for them. The lower bound comes from representations of the knot group in $\GL_4(\F_q)$ that send a meridian to a transvection or a reflection and fix no nonzero vector. KnotInfo leaves the smooth nonorientable four-genus open for 
total{} prime knots with eleven to thirteen crossings; we determine it for 
settled{} of them and narrow the interval for 
narrowed{} more. Upper bounds come from pinch moves, lower bounds from the Goeritz-lattice obstructions of Jabuka and Kelly evaluated by an exhaustive search for lattice embeddings. Every bound is a certificate checked by a program independent of the search that found it.

papers.title: The classification of smooth 3-fold flops
papers.abstract: This paper establishes the analytic classification of smooth, simple, 3-fold flops, and in the process provides both an intrinsic characterisation and a classification of their contraction algebras.

papers.title: The dual complex and RC-invariant functors
papers.abstract: We extend the dual complex of a simple normal crossings divisor to a homotopy type invariant $\mathcal{D}(X)$ of arbitrary complex varieties, and we prove that it is contractible when $X$ is connected and of klt type. In fact, the dual complex belongs to a broader class of invariants, which we call RC (rationally connected)-invariant functors. We prove a rigidity theorem governing the behavior of such functors with respect to rationally connected fibrations.

papers.title: The Game-Theoretic Kat\v{e}tov Order and Idealised Effective Subtoposes
papers.abstract:
This paper addresses the longstanding problem of determining the structure of the $\leq_{\mathrm{LT}}$-order in the Effective Topos, known to effectively embed the Turing degrees. In a surprising discovery, we show that the $\leq_{\mathrm{LT}}$-order is in fact tightly controlled by the combinatorics of filters on $\omega$, raising deep questions about how combinatorial and computable complexity interact, both within this order and beyond it.
  To make the connection precise, we introduce a game-theoretic (''gamified'') variant of the Kat\v{e}tov order on filters over $\omega$, which turns out to exhibit a striking mix of coarseness and subtlety. For one, it is strictly coarser than the classical Rudin-Keisler order and, when viewed dually on ideals, collapses all MAD families to a single equivalence class. On the other hand, the order also supports a rich internal structure, including an infinite strictly ascending chain of ideal classes, which we identify by way of a new separation technique.
  From the computability-theoretic perspective, we show that a computable (and extended) variant of the gamified Kat\v{e}tov order is isomorphic to the original $\leq_{\mathrm{LT}}$-order. Moreover, our work brings into focus a new degree-spectrum invariant for filters $\mathcal{F}$, $$\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{T}}(\mathcal{F}):=\{\,[f\colon\omega\to\omega] \mid f\leq_{\mathrm{LT}} \mathcal{F} \},$$
  which is shown to always determine a proper initial segment of the Turing degrees. Extending this, given any non-principal $\Delta^1_1$ filter $\mathcal{F}$, we show that $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{T}}(\mathcal{F})$ is precisely the class of hyperarithmetic degrees. This significantly generalises previous results obtained by van Oosten \cite{vO14} and Kihara \cite{Kih23}.
  The proofs draw on ideas from general topology, descriptive set theory, and computability theory.

papers.title: The generic splitting type of the logarithmic bundle of an arrangement of at most sixteen lines is combinatorial
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an arrangement of $d$ lines in $\mathbb{P}^2_\mathbb{C}$ and let $\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}angle$ be its bundle of logarithmic vector fields. On a general line, $\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}angle$ splits as $\mathcal{O}(-k)\oplus\mathcal{O}(k+1-d)$ with $k=\min\{\mathrm{mdr}(\mathcal{A}),\lfloor rac{d-1}{2}floor\}$, where $\mathrm{mdr}$ is the minimal degree of a Jacobian syzygy. We prove that $k$ is determined by the intersection lattice whenever $d\le16$, answering in this range a question of Cook, Harbourne, Migliore and Nagel. Since freeness can be read off from $k$ and $c_2(\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}angle)$, this strengthens Terao's freeness conjecture in this range; in particular we obtain a proof of Terao's conjecture for $14$ lines that uses it only for $13$ lines. For any number $d$ of lines, it follows that $\mathrm{mdr}$ is determined by the lattice whenever $\mathrm{mdr}\le6$ and $2\mathrm{mdr}\le d-3$, and that Terao's conjecture holds for every free arrangement whose smaller exponent is at most $7$.
  The proof reduces the question to critical arrangements: $2s+3$ lines, each containing at most $s+1$ intersection points, with $\mathrm{mdr}=s$. For these, the inflection polynomial of the minimal derivation factors as $Q_\mathcal{A} R$ with $R\in H^0(\mathcal{I}_Z^2(s-3))$, where $Z$ is the zero scheme of the derivation, of length $
u=c_2(\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}angle)-s(s+2)$. For $s\le5$ this forces $
u\le1$, and Chern class arguments then reduce everything to Terao's conjecture for $13$ lines. For $s=6$ we show $
u\le3$, using a Riccati equation along multiple components of $R$, Ziegler's multirestriction, and local computations verified by computer algebra; an exhaustive enumeration of the 26,265,318 candidate lattices with $
u\in\{2,3\}$ that satisfy Bojanowski's inequality completes the proof.

papers.title: The minimum number of distinct abelian squares in a binary circular word
papers.abstract: We prove that every binary circular word of length $n$ contains at least $\fl{(n-1)/2}$ distinct abelian squares, and we determine all words attaining this bound. This settles a conjecture of Simpson: its odd case holds, and in its even case the list of extremal words misses $(ab)^{n/2}$ for $n\equiv 2\pmod 4$, $n\ge 6$.

papers.title: The Number of Terms in Greedy Fibonacci--Lucas Representations
papers.abstract: We prove Kimberling's conjecture on greedy representations by Fibonacci and Lucas numbers: the ratio of the number of Zeckendorf summands of $1,\dots,n$ to the number of terms of their greedy representations tends to a limit in $(1.2,1.4)$, and the limit is $(5-\sqrt5)/2$. We also prove the conjectures of Greathouse and Kurkov on the number of terms of the greedy representation.

papers.title: The Penrose Correspondence over a Non-Archimedean Field
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic different from $2$ and let $V$ be a four-dimensional symplectic $K$-vector space. We study the Penrose incidence correspondence $\mathbb{P}(V) \leftarrow \mathrm{Flag}(1,2;V) \rightarrow \mathrm{Gr}(2,V)$ after Berkovich analytification. The Klein quadric $\mathrm{Gr}(2,V)$ decomposes into the open orbit $\mathrm{Spin}(5)/\mathrm{Spin}(4)$ and the Lagrangian quadric, which parametrize respectively the projective lines transverse and tangent to the standard contact distribution on $\mathbb{P}(V)$. We construct explicit free discrete subgroups $\Gamma\subset\mathrm{PSp}(V)$ and analytic domains, cut out by Drinfeld upper half-spaces, in all three members of the incidence diagram. Both incidence projections are surjective on these domains, the three $\Gamma$-actions are free and properly discontinuous, and the Penrose double correspondence descends to the analytic quotients. The quotient of the twistor domain is a contact analytic threefold, and the Grassmannian domain is contained in the analytification of the $\mathrm{Spin}(5)/\mathrm{Spin}(4)$ open orbit.

papers.title: The Real-Rooting Time Of Heat-Evolved Random Polynomials
papers.abstract: Let $G_{n,t}=\exp(-\frac{t}{2n}\partial_z^2)G_n$ be a random Weyl polynomial of degree $n$ under the backward heat flow, with independent coefficients of a law that is not a point mass and has finite variance. Hall, Ho, Jalowy and Kabluchko showed that the empirical zero distribution collapses onto the real line at $t=1$. We show that the first time at which all zeros of $G_{n,t}$ are real, a finite-degree analogue of the de Bruijn--Newman constant, converges in distribution to $T_*=R_*^{-2}$, where $R_*$ is the smallest modulus of a nonreal zero of the random power series $\sum_j\eta_jw^j$ with coefficients of the same law; the convergence is almost sure under a coupling of the degrees that shares the top coefficients, whereas under the standard coupling the set of limit points of the real-rooting time is almost surely $[1,\infty]$. The proof rests on an exact count of the nonreal zeros of analytic combinations $\sum_{j\le n}a_jh_{n-j}$ of orthonormal Hermite polynomials: if the real power series $a$ has radius of convergence greater than $1$, no zeros on the unit circle and simple zeros in the unit disk, then for all large $n$ the combination has exactly as many nonreal zeros as $a$ has in the disk. Its method expresses the polynomial and its derivative in the bulk through a $2\times2$ matrix applied to $(h_n,h_{n-1})$, built from only $O(\log n)$ steps of the backward three-term recurrence, with the remaining terms controlled by a Christoffel--Darboux bound. For Gaussian coefficients the law of $T_*$ is a Fredholm determinant, $\mathbb{P}(T_*>t)\sim\frac4{3\pi}t^{-3/2}$ as $t\to\infty$, and $(t-1)\log\mathbb{P}(T_*\le t)\to-\pi^2/12$ as $t\downarrow1$, half of the constant for complex coefficients. At the scale $1/n$ the last pair of nonreal zeros collides inside the real bulk, at relative position $\cos\theta_*$, where $R_*e^{\pm i\theta_*}$ are the nonreal zeros of minimal modulus, and the real-rooting time is within $O(1/n)$ of $T_*$. In a window of size $1/n$ the polynomial is, up to a positive factor and $O(1/n)$, the model $\zeta\cos(\zeta+c)+\lambda\sin(\zeta+c)$, whose threshold for real-rootedness is given by Kepler's equation; the phase $c$ rotates with $n$, so $n(\Lambda_n-T_*)$ oscillates over an explicit interval and has an explicit limit law jointly with $T_*$.

papers.title: The Sch\"utzenberger involution and colored lattice models
papers.abstract:
Colored lattice models can be used to describe many different types of special functions of interest in both algebraic combinatorics and representation theory, for example Schur polynomials, nonsymmetric Macdonald polynomials, and characters and Whittaker functions for representations of p-adic groups. A notable example is the metaplectic ice model of which there are actually two different variants: a Gamma and a Delta variant. These variants differ in key aspects but surprisingly produce equal partition functions, which are weighted sums over admissible configurations, and this equality is called the Gamma-Delta duality. The duality was used to prove the analytic continuation of certain multiple Dirichlet series and is highly non-trivial, especially since the number of configurations on each side of the equality can differ.
  In this paper we generalize the Gamma-Delta duality by constructing a new family of solvable, colored lattice models and prove that they are dual to existing lattice models in the literature. Besides the above metaplectic case we also get a new lattice model and Gamma-Delta type duality for (non-metaplectic) Iwahori Whittaker functions together with a crystal limit for Demazure atoms for Cartan type A. The equality of partition functions is shown using Yang-Baxter equations involving both variants of lattice models simultaneously.
  For the crystal lattice model we show that the duality refines to a weight-respecting bijection of states given by the Sch\"utzenberger involution on the associated Gelfand-Tsetlin patterns or semistandard Young tableaux. We also show how the individual steps exchanging two rows in the proof of the duality for the partition functions refines to Berenstein-Kirillov or, equivalently, Bender-Knuth involutions.

papers.title: The shifted symplectic geometry of derived higher groupoids
papers.abstract: The main goal of this work is to introduce derived Lie n-groupoids and their shifted symplectic structures. We further define shifted lagrangian structures and prove that their composition is well defined under suitable conditions. As an application, we show that our framework incorporates several reduction procedures at critical values, including: classical Hamiltonian reduction, group valued moment maps, Poisson Lie group valued moment maps and Mikami-Weinstein for proper symplectic groupoids.

papers.title: The symmetric skew monoidal structure of Gray-categories
papers.abstract: In a previous paper, we constructed a closed skew monoidal structure on the category of Gray-categories and Gray-functors whose internal hom Psd(A, B) captures pseudomaps and pseudo-transformations. In the present paper we give a symmetric description of the Gray-category Psd(A,B) and use this to prove that the skew monoidal structure is symmetric skew monoidal.

papers.title: The symplectic isotopy problem for rational cuspidal curves
papers.abstract: We define a suitably tame class of singular symplectic curves in 4-manifolds, namely those whose singularities are modeled on complex curve singularities. We study the corresponding symplectic isotopy problem, with a focus on rational curves with irreducible singularities (rational cuspidal curves) in the complex projective plane. We prove that every such curve is isotopic to a complex curve in degrees up to 5, and for curves with one singularity whose link is a torus knot. Classification results of symplectic isotopy classes rely on pseudo-holomorphic curves together with a symplectic version of birational geometry of log pairs and techniques from 4-dimensional topology.

papers.title: The symplectic leaves of the affine Poisson $C^\infty$-scheme associated with a singular subalgebroid
papers.abstract: Every singular subalgebroid, and in particular every singular foliation $\mathscr{G}$, determines a universal Poisson $C^\infty$-scheme $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$, which is the analogue of the linear Poisson structure on the dual of a Lie algebroid. We show that the underlying space $X_{\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G})}$ of $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$ decomposes as a disjoint union of symplectic manifolds. Furthermore, we extend the Helffer-Nourrigat cone to a singular subalgebroid and show that it is an embedded Poisson $C^\infty$-subscheme of $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$.

papers.title: The taming of 3-fold flops
papers.abstract: This article overviews recent progress in understanding and classifying one of the most elementary of birational surgeries within algebraic geometry, namely 3-fold flops, through the development of a noncommutative version of singularity theory.

papers.title: The Welch function is not third-order sum-free
papers.abstract: Let $n=2m+1$. Hou and Zhao conjectured that for $n\ge7$ the Welch function $X^{2^m+3}$ on $\F_{2^n}$ sums to zero over some three-dimensional affine subspace, that is, it is not third-order sum-free. We prove this. The proof counts exactly the elements $x$ for which some subspace spanned by $1$, $x$ and a third element gives a zero sum: there are $(2^n+1-3K_n)/4$ of them, where $K_n$ is a binary Kloosterman sum.

papers.title: Third-Order Weierstrass Points on Plane Quartics
papers.abstract: For a smooth plane quartic $C$, the $3$-Weierstrass points are the $300$ points (counted with weights) at which some plane cubic has contact order at least ten with $C$. Revisiting the work of Kamel and Elshareef, we write the third Veronese Wronskian as an $\text{SL}_3$-covariant form $\Omega_3$ of degree $75$, given by a determinant of iterated Hamiltonian derivatives, and explain the special $3$-Weierstrass points through contact cubics and homologies preserving $C$. We determine $\Omega_3$ for the Fermat, Komiya--Kuribayashi, Klein and Picard quartics; for the Klein quartic $\Omega_3\equiv\Phi_6^2\,\Phi_{21}\,(3\Phi_{14}^3+21962\,\Phi_6^7)$ modulo the curve, up to a non-zero scalar. Finally, the dectactic points of the Fermat quartic are not $4$-Weierstrass points, which disproves a conjecture of Kamel and Elshareef. All computations are supported by \texttt{SINGULAR} scripts.

papers.title: Three-dimensional noncommutative Fano minifolds
papers.abstract: We give a construction of the previously announced family of three-dimensional noncommutative Fano minifolds of Euler degree $72$. We prove that their defining $\mathbb{Z}$-algebras are Koszul and Artin--Schelter regular, and compute the Hilbert series of their section algebras.

papers.title: Three-periodic helices on elliptic curves and their associated regular algebras
papers.abstract: Let $k$ denote an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and let $X$ denote a smooth elliptic curve over $k$. Given a three-periodic elliptic helix $\underline{\mathcal{E}}$ of vector bundles over $X$ with endomorphism $\mathbb{Z}$-algebra $\operatorname{End} \underline{\mathcal{E}}$ and quadratic cover $\mathbb{S}^{nc}(\underline{\mathcal{E}})$, we prove that $\operatorname{End} \underline{\mathcal{E}}$ is the quotient of $\mathbb{S}^{nc}(\underline{\mathcal{E}})$ by a degree three family of normal elements, generalizing a result of the authors to the case in which $\operatorname{dim }(\operatorname{End} \underline{\mathcal{E}})_{i, i+1}$ isn't a constant function of $i$. We then show that $\operatorname{End} \underline{\mathcal{E}}$ is noetherian if and only if it has polynomial growth, and in this case, the ranks of any three consecutive bundles in the helix are a Markov triple. Furthermore, in this case $\mathbb{S}^{nc}(\underline{\mathcal{E}})$ is a noetherian GK-three $\mathbb{Z}$-algebra which is ${\sf Proj }$-equivalent to an elliptic algebra. We conclude the paper by constructing several new families of elliptic helices with exponential growth.

papers.title: Triple Quantum Schubert Calculus
papers.abstract: We prove a triple quantum Pieri formula: the product of a quantum double Schubert polynomial $\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_u(x;y)$ by a quantum factorial elementary polynomial $\widetilde{E}_{p,k}(x;z)$ in a second set of variables $z$ is a sum over chains in the quantum Bruhat graph, indexed by a quantum analogue of Sottile's relation, whose coefficients are monomials in the quantum parameters times polynomials in the differences $y_i-z_j$ with nonnegative integer coefficients, and which is Graham-positive at $z=y$. At $y=z=0$ it is the quantum Pieri rule of Ciocan-Fontanine and Postnikov; at $z=y$ it is an equivariant quantum Pieri rule for the complete flag variety, indexed by chains in the quantum Bruhat graph rather than, as in the rule of Huang and Li, by the data of a reduction to classical cohomology, and proved directly. A doubled Pieri formula, positive in the same senses, treats multiplication by the quantization of a product of two elementary polynomials in the same variables, which is not the product of the quantizations: it is two iterated Pieri steps with the incompatible pairs of chains omitted. More generally, the triple quantum Schubert structure constants $c_{u,v}^{w,d}(y;z)$, the coefficients of $\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_u(x;y)\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_v(x;z)$ in the basis $\{\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_w(x;y)\}$, are polynomials in the $y_i-z_j$ with nonnegative integer coefficients; the proof of this appears as an appendix. We extend the Peterson-Woodward comparison formula and the quantum-to-classical reduction of Leung-Li and Huang-Li to the triple constants, and we describe and prove correct the algorithms of schubmult, which compute products of arbitrary quantum double Schubert polynomials well beyond the reach of previous methods.

papers.title: Two conjectures of Wormald on Hamilton cycles in tournaments
papers.abstract: For a regular tournament on $d$ vertices with skew adjacency matrix $S$, the Hessian determinant $H$ that Wormald attached to its random blow-ups equals $d\det(d^2I+S^2)/\det(d^2I-S^2)$. Hence $H\neq0$ and $d/H$ is the square of a rational number, as Wormald conjectured. For the cyclic tournament it gives $\sqrt{d/H}=\bigl((d+1)^d+(d-1)^d\bigr)/\bigl((d+i)^d+(d-i)^d\bigr)$, so the associated constants tend to $\cosh 1/\cos 1=2.8559578925\ldots$; this proves a second conjecture of Wormald and identifies his numerical constant.

papers.title: Uniformity of the minimal exponent on the GIT boundary of projective hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a non-stable (in the sense of GIT) hypersurface of degree $d \ge 3$ in the projective space $\mathbb{P}^{n}$. S. G. Park proved that the global minimal exponent of $X$ satisfies the inequality $\widetilde{\alpha}(X) \le \frac{n+1}{d}$. In this paper, we establish the uniform sharpness of this inequality: we prove that $\widetilde{\alpha}(X) = \frac{n+1}{d}$ holds for a general member $X$ of every irreducible component of the strictly semistable locus. Moreover, a general point of each irreducible component of the GIT boundary $\partial M^{\mathrm{GIT}}$ admits a strictly semistable zero-weight representative with this minimal exponent. By the lower semicontinuity of the minimal exponent on the affine cone and a theorem of Musta\c{t}\u{a}--Popa for general linear combinations of monomials, the problem is reduced to computing the log canonical thresholds, at the cone vertex, of the monomial ideals associated with the maximal strictly semistable supports with respect to a maximal torus and their weight-zero parts. Since the barycenter of the degree-$d$ simplex lies in the convex hull of each of these supports, Howald's formula forces these thresholds to be uniformly equal to $\frac{n+1}{d}$.

papers.title: Unipotent representations and the categorical trace of Frobenius
papers.abstract: We give a new proof of the classification of unipotent representations for split finite groups of Lie type. To do this, we first construct an (infinity, 2)-categorification of Lusztig's map from the Hecke algebra to the asymptotic algebra. Then we use the theory of weights to show that it induces an isomorphism after applying trace of Frobenius.

papers.title: Weil classes on abelian sixfolds of Weil type for $\mathbb{Q}(i)$ with discriminant $-3$
papers.abstract: Let $K=\mathbb{Q}(i)$. We prove that the Weil classes of every polarized complex abelian sixfold of Weil type for $K$ whose Hermitian discriminant is the non-split class $[-3]$ are algebraic, and that every Hodge class on every power of such a sixfold is algebraic when its Hodge group is the full special unitary group. The proof starts from Galois covers of the projective line with monodromy group $W(E_8)\cdot\mu_4$, branched over twelve points: the multiplicity space of the natural representation in the cohomology of such a cover is the first cohomology of an abelian sixfold of Weil type, and a certified rank computation at one explicit cover shows that these sixfolds fill an open set of the nine-dimensional moduli space. Algebraic cycles reach these sixfolds through Milne's theorem on Lefschetz classes, from two sources: Schoen's cycles on cyclic covers, which a computer search shows do not suffice here, and products of determinant lines of characters on abelian covers of curves. For the second source we prove a general theorem (Theorem C): if such a product is of Hodge type at every Galois conjugate, and each of the cyclic covers involved has at least two branch points and order dividing $12$ after removing the common factor of its branch exponents, then the product spans a space of algebraic classes. Its proof runs Schoen's symmetric-product construction on each factor, localises at a special fibre, transfers to a product of Fermat hypersurfaces, and applies Shioda's theorem on products of Fermat varieties. This version is archived on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23566607; its computational certificates: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23549514

papers.title: Weyl chambers, asymptotic expansions, and blowup analysis of explicit Toda solutions
papers.abstract: Blowup analysis is a central part of geometric analysis, and systems of PDEs such as Toda systems exhibit particularly rich blowup behavior. In [Nie25], the author constructed explicit families of radial Toda solutions whose blowup masses correspond to arbitrary elements of the Weyl group of the underlying Lie algebra. In this paper, we study these families within the framework of blowup analysis developed by C.-S. Lin and his coauthors. The key is an asymptotic analysis of the solution family that distinguishes Cartan elements in the interior of a Weyl chamber from those lying on its boundary faces. We prove a uniform upper bound for $u_i^{\lambda,H}(r)+2\log r$, so that the selection estimate holds with the center at the origin. We show that the successive bubbling scales for slow decay are determined by the intersections of the ray $H+tq_\mu$ with root hyperplanes. At each crossing, rescaling and the face asymptotics identify the limiting profiles as explicit solutions of the corresponding Levi-Toda subsystems. The masses of these successive bubbles, computed using [KLNW24], account for the entire blowup mass. Examples in type $A_2$ demonstrate this identification and exhibit both separated scalar bubbles and a simultaneous full-system bubble.

papers.title: Which String Vibrations Become Which Generations on the Dwork Quintic
papers.abstract: We determine, for the heterotic string on the one-parameter family of quintic threefolds, which vibration modes become which families of charged particles. The hundred and one families are labelled by the characters of a symmetry group of order one hundred and twenty-five. Every Yukawa coupling that this symmetry allows is a power of the modulus, and every other coupling vanishes. The invariant deformation pairs each family with exactly one partner, so that fifty families are massless at the Fermat point and none anywhere else, and at the Fermat point the masses are given in closed form by the Gamma function. On the three other one-parameter families of the same type, in weighted projective spaces, the symmetry no longer tells the families apart and some families stay massless at every member. We also prove that the Geometric Selection Conjecture is equivalent to the existence of one viable vacuum fixed by mirror symmetry, and that a free quotient of a Calabi–Yau complete intersection of any of the thirteen one-parameter hypergeometric types never carries three families with the standard embedding; on seven of these types, among them the sextic and dectic pencils, no finite group acts freely at all.
